Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

consistent adjective

consistent with, in keeping with

also consistent with, in keeping with, agree with (of facts), inconsistent with, tally

classical

Cic. Fam. 3.6.2 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Phil. 9.15: mors ejus vītae sānctissimē āctae

cōnsentāneus, cōnsentānea, cōnsentāneum

adjective; with cum or the dative

agreeing with, in keeping with

Cicero’s word above all (Lewis & Short); it also means fitting, proper.

Other words

  • congruēns, congruentis — agreeing, consistent, appropriate

    adjective, third declension; with cum or the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 117: vīta cum disciplīnā (Lewis & Short, s.v. congruō); Cic. Leg. 1.30: ōrātiō verbīs discrepāns, sententiīs congruēns

    From congruō, “come together, coincide”.

  • conveniō cum (+ abl.) — to agree with, fit

    verb, fourth conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · conveniēns: Cic. Off. 1.58 (Lewis & Short)

    Hoc nōn convenit cum eō quod dīxistī: “this isn’t consistent with what you said”.

Examples

  • quod quidem erat cōnsentāneum cum iīs litterīs, quās ego Rōmae accēperam

    which was indeed consistent with the letter I had received at RomeCic. Fam. 3.6.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • ōrātiō verbīs discrepāns, sententiīs congruēns

    a speech differing in its words but consistent in its thoughtsCic. Leg. 1.30 (Lewis & Short)

  • Hoc nōn convenit cum eō quod heri dīxistī.

    This isn’t consistent with what you said yesterday.composed

See also consistent, agree, reasonable.

SourcesLewis & Short: consentaneus · Lewis & Short: congruo · Lewis & Short: convenio

Cicero quoted as Lewis & Short quotes him.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
